title: Gene Ammons joins in Cincinnati; Lucky Thompson the clean-cut straight man
summary: Ammons becomes a spark of the band, while Lucky Thompson is sober, well dressed and serious.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Back to where we were. I think the last city I mentioned was Cleveland. I think we went from Cleveland to Cincinnati. This is where Gene Ammons was... I think Gene was about 18 years old or 19 when he joined the band, and became the tenor saxophone player that lasted through the whole existence of the band, and became one of the major sparks in the band. Anyone that listens to it will understand what I'm saying.
Because the other tenor saxophone player at that particular time was Lucky Thompson. Lucky Thompson at that

particular time... I haven't seen him in quite a number of years. But he was a very clean-cut young man. He dressed well, and he didn't smoke, he didn't drink, and he was very serious about his music. He was a good saxophone player, and always stayed sharp. He used to use this hair straightener that was popular then, that all the Black guys were using, which straightened your hair and made it look straight and slick and everything. Certain guys could do it very well, and it looked very good. And Lucky Thompson was one. His hair always looked beautiful. On the bandstand he was always dressed well, and in the hot weather he would have a towel around his neck. But as I said before, his behavior, compared to what some of the other guys were doing, he was a real straight guy. He didn't drink, he didn't smoke, and very seldom did you hear him swear at anything.
